title: 🧩 Game 8: Odd One Out (10 Progressive Levels · 150 Intruder Sets)
subtitle: 10 Progressive Levels · 150 Curated Questions · 100% Verified UGC NET Content

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following novels was NOT written by Charles Dickens?
items.explanation: Middlemarch (1871–72) was written by George Eliot (Mary Ann Evans). Bleak House (1853), Great Expectations (1861), and Hard Times (1854) are all major Victorian social novels by Charles Dickens.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following Elizabethan/Jacobean dramas was NOT written by William Shakespeare?
items.explanation: Doctor Faustus (c. 1592) was written by Christopher Marlowe. The Tempest (1611), Othello (1603), and King Lear (1606) are canonical masterpieces of William Shakespeare.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following Regency novels was NOT written by Jane Austen?
items.explanation: Jane Eyre (1847) was written by Charlotte Brontë (under the pen name Currer Bell). Pride and Prejudice (1813), Persuasion (1817), and Mansfield Park (1814) were all written by Jane Austen.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following 17th-century works was NOT written by John Milton?
items.explanation: Absalom and Achitophel (1681) is a political heroic-couplet satire by John Dryden. Paradise Lost (1667), Samson Agonistes (1671), and Lycidas (1637) are celebrated works by John Milton.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following Middle English works was NOT composed by Geoffrey Chaucer?
items.explanation: Piers Plowman is an allegorical alliterative dream vision written by William Langland. The Canterbury Tales, Troilus and Criseyde, and The Book of the Duchess are seminal works by Geoffrey Chaucer.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following Augustan satirical works was NOT written by Jonathan Swift?
items.explanation: The Rape of the Lock (1712/1714) is a mock-heroic narrative poem by Alexander Pope. Gulliver's Travels (1726), A Tale of a Tub (1704), and The Battle of the Books (1704) are classic prose satires by Jonathan Swift.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian rural novels was NOT written by Thomas Hardy?
items.explanation: Adam Bede (1859) was George Eliot's first full-length novel. Tess of the d'Urbervilles (1891), Jude the Obscure (1895), and The Mayor of Casterbridge (1886) are tragic Wessex novels by Thomas Hardy.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following early 20th-century novels was NOT written by Virginia Woolf?
items.explanation: The Rainbow (1915) was written by D. H. Lawrence. Mrs Dalloway (1925), To the Lighthouse (1927), and Orlando (1928) are landmark modernist novels by Virginia Woolf.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #9
items.stem: Which of the following 20th-century political and social works was NOT written by George Orwell?
options: Down and Out in Paris and London
items.explanation: Brave New World (1932) is a dystopian novel by Aldous Huxley. Nineteen Eighty-Four (1949), Animal Farm (1945), and Down and Out in Paris and London (1933) were all written by George Orwell.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following major Romantic odes was NOT composed by John Keats?
items.explanation: Ode to the West Wind (1819) was written in terza rima by Percy Bysshe Shelley. Ode to a Nightingale, Ode on a Grecian Urn, and To Autumn are famous 1819 odes composed by John Keats.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following Romantic poems was NOT composed by William Wordsworth?
options: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
items.explanation: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner (1798) was composed by Samuel Taylor Coleridge. The Prelude, Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey, and The Solitary Reaper are canonical poems by William Wordsworth.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #12
items.meta: Major Poetic Works of Lord Byron
items.stem: Which of the following Romantic verse dramas or long poems was NOT written by Lord Byron?
items.explanation: Prometheus Unbound (1820) is a lyrical drama by Percy Bysshe Shelley. Don Juan (1819–24), Childe Harold's Pilgrimage (1812–18), and Manfred (1817) were composed by Lord Byron.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following 19th-century novels was NOT written by Charlotte Brontë?
items.explanation: Wuthering Heights (1847) was written by Emily Brontë (Ellis Bell). Jane Eyre (1847), Villette (1853), and Shirley (1849) were all written by Charlotte Brontë (Currer Bell).

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following 18th-century masterpieces was NOT written by Alexander Pope?
items.explanation: The School for Scandal (1777) is a celebrated comedy of manners written by Richard Brinsley Sheridan. The Rape of the Lock, The Dunciad, and An Essay on Criticism are major verse works by Alexander Pope.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 1 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following Renaissance stage works was NOT written by Ben Jonson?
items.explanation: The Jew of Malta (c. 1589) is a tragedy written by Christopher Marlowe. Volpone (1606), The Alchemist (1610), and Every Man in His Humour (1598) are famous Jacobean comedies written by Ben Jonson.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following Elizabethan dramatists was NOT one of the 'University Wits'?
items.explanation: William Shakespeare did not attend Oxford or Cambridge and was famously attacked by University Wit Robert Greene as an 'upstart Crow'. Christopher Marlowe, Robert Greene, and Thomas Nashe were all Cambridge- or Oxford-educated University Wits.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following 17th-century poets was NOT a Metaphysical poet?
items.explanation: Robert Herrick was a leading Cavalier poet ('Sons of Ben') and author of Hesperides. John Donne, George Herbert, and Andrew Marvell are central figures of the Metaphysical school of poetry.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following Caroline-era poets was NOT one of the Cavalier poets?
items.explanation: Henry Vaughan was a Welsh Metaphysical devotional poet deeply influenced by George Herbert. Richard Lovelace, Sir John Suckling, and Thomas Carew were courtier Cavalier poets dedicated to King Charles I.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following Jacobean theatrical works is NOT a revenge tragedy?
items.explanation: The Alchemist (1610) by Ben Jonson is a satirical city comedy. The Duchess of Malfi (Webster), The Revenger's Tragedy (Middleton/Tourneur), and The White Devil (Webster) are quintessential Jacobean revenge tragedies.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following Elizabethan poetic works is NOT a sonnet sequence?
items.explanation: The Faerie Queene by Edmund Spenser is an epic chivalric allegory composed in Spenserian stanzas. Astrophil and Stella (Sidney), Amoretti (Spenser), and Delia (Daniel) are all prominent Elizabethan sonnet sequences.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following Renaissance court masques was NOT written by Ben Jonson?
items.explanation: Comus (1634) is a masque written by John Milton with music by Henry Lawes. The Masque of Blackness, The Masque of Queens, and Pleasure Reconciled to Virtue were all written by Ben Jonson in collaboration with Inigo Jones.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following Shakespearean plays is NOT categorized as one of his Roman Plays?
items.explanation: Pericles, Prince of Tyre is a late romance based on Hellenistic and medieval legends. Julius Caesar, Antony and Cleopatra, and Coriolanus are Shakespeare's classical Roman tragedies based on Thomas North's translation of Plutarch's Lives.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following dramas is NOT traditionally categorized among Shakespeare's 'Problem Plays'?
items.explanation: The Tempest is a late romance/pastoral tragicomedy. Measure for Measure, Troilus and Cressida, and All's Well That Ends Well are the dark comedies famously defined as 'Problem Plays' by F. S. Boas.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #9
items.stem: Which of the following Elizabethan works was NOT authored by Edmund Spenser?
items.explanation: Euphues: The Anatomy of Wit (1578) is a didactic prose romance by John Lyly that gave rise to 'euphuism'. The Faerie Queene, The Shepheardes Calender, and Epithalamion are foundational works by Edmund Spenser.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following Renaissance plays was NOT written by Christopher Marlowe?
items.explanation: The Spanish Tragedy (c. 1587) was written by Thomas Kyd and established the English revenge tragedy formula. Tamburlaine the Great, The Jew of Malta, and Edward II were written by Christopher Marlowe.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following literary figures was NOT a major Jacobean playwright?
items.explanation: Sir Philip Sidney was an Elizabethan courtier, poet, and critic who died in 1586, long before the Jacobean era began in 1603. John Webster, Thomas Middleton, and John Fletcher were prolific Jacobean dramatists.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #12
items.stem: Which of the following Elizabethan literary works is NOT a pastoral prose romance?
items.explanation: The Spanish Tragedy is a blank-verse revenge tragedy by Thomas Kyd. Arcadia (Sidney), Pandosto (Greene, source of The Winter's Tale), and Rosalynde (Lodge, source of As You Like It) are pastoral prose romances.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following stage plays is NOT one of William Shakespeare's English chronicle histories?
items.explanation: The White Devil (1612) is an Italianate Jacobean tragedy by John Webster. Richard II, Henry IV, Part 1, and Henry V form core parts of Shakespeare's celebrated historical 'Henriad' tetralogies.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following figures was NOT a 16th-century Tudor humanist or early prose translator?
items.explanation: Richard Crashaw was a 17th-century Caroline Metaphysical poet and Catholic convert. Thomas More (Utopia), William Tyndale (Bible translation), and Roger Ascham (The Scholemaster) were key 16th-century Tudor humanists.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 2 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following Elizabethan narrative works is NOT an epyllion (mythological minor epic)?
items.explanation: Astrophil and Stella by Sir Philip Sidney is a petrarchan sonnet sequence. Venus and Adonis (Shakespeare), Hero and Leander (Marlowe), and The Scourge of Venus (Barksted) are erotic mythological narrative poems known as epyllia.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following Augustan writers was NOT a member of the Scriblerus Club?
items.explanation: Daniel Defoe was a Whig journalist and dissenter who was frequently satirized and ridiculed by the Tory Scriblerians. Alexander Pope, Jonathan Swift, John Gay, and John Arbuthnot were core Scriblerus Club founders.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following 18th-century poets was NOT one of the 'Graveyard Poets'?
items.explanation: John Dryden was the dominant Restoration Neoclassical poet laureate who died in 1700. Thomas Gray ('Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'), Edward Young (Night-Thoughts), and Robert Blair (The Grave) were the Graveyard Poets.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following Restoration dramatic works is NOT a comedy of manners?
items.explanation: Venice Preserv'd (1682) by Thomas Otway is a Restoration heroic blank-verse tragedy. The Country Wife (Wycherley), The Way of the World (Congreve), and The Man of Mode (Etherege) are quintessential Restoration comedies of manners.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following Restoration stage works was NOT authored by John Dryden?
items.explanation: The Rover (1677) is a Restoration comedy of intrigue written by Aphra Behn. The Conquest of Granada, Aureng-Zebe, and All for Love are leading heroic and tragic dramas written by John Dryden.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following Augustan publications was NOT a periodical essay or journal?
items.explanation: The Dunciad is a mock-heroic satirical verse epic composed by Alexander Pope. The Tatler (Steele), The Spectator (Addison and Steele), and The Rambler (Samuel Johnson) were prominent 18th-century periodical essay series.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following poetic works is NOT a mock-heroic satire?
items.explanation: Paradise Lost by John Milton is a grand, serious Christian theological epic in blank verse. The Rape of the Lock (Pope), Mac Flecknoe (Dryden), and The Dunciad (Pope) are celebrated mock-heroic satires in heroic couplets.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following 18th-century British novels is NOT written in epistolary form?
items.explanation: The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling (1749) by Henry Fielding is a picaresque comic epic in prose featuring an intrusive omniscient narrator. Pamela, Clarissa (both by Richardson), and Evelina (by Burney) are epistolary novels.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following 18th-century novels is NOT an episodic picaresque or adventure novel?
items.explanation: The Castle of Otranto (1764) by Horace Walpole is the foundational Gothic romance novel. Roderick Random (Smollett), Peregrine Pickle (Smollett), and Moll Flanders (Defoe) are classic picaresque/adventure narratives.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #9
items.stem: Which of the following 18th-century figures was NOT a member of Samuel Johnson's 'The Club'?
items.explanation: William Blake was a radical, visionary poet and engraver who operated outside mainstream London circles. Oliver Goldsmith, Edmund Burke, and Sir Joshua Reynolds were prominent founding members of Johnson's Literary Club (formed 1764).

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following 18th-century works is NOT a novel of sensibility (sentimental novel)?
items.explanation: The Monk (1796) by Matthew Gregory Lewis is a sensational Gothic horror novel. The Man of Feeling (Mackenzie), A Sentimental Journey (Sterne), and The Vicar of Wakefield (Goldsmith) are benchmark works of 18th-century sensibility.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following Augustan authors was NOT primarily recognized as a satirist?
items.explanation: James Thomson was a Scottish pre-Romantic poet famous for his expansive descriptive blank-verse nature poem The Seasons. Alexander Pope, Jonathan Swift, and John Arbuthnot were prominent satirists of the Augustan Age.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #12
items.stem: Which of the following female authors was NOT an 18th-century novelist or Bluestocking figure?
items.explanation: Aphra Behn was a Restoration-era playwright and novelist who died in 1689. Frances Burney (Evelina), Charlotte Lennox (The Female Quixote), and Elizabeth Carter were notable 18th-century writers and Bluestocking associates.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following critical essays was NOT authored by John Dryden?
items.explanation: An Essay on Criticism (1711) is a verse treatise in heroic couplets written by Alexander Pope. Of Dramatic Poesy (1668), Preface to the Fables (1700), and Essay on Heroic Plays (1672) were written by John Dryden.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following early British novels was NOT written by Daniel Defoe?
items.explanation: Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded (1740) was written by Samuel Richardson. Robinson Crusoe (1719), Moll Flanders (1722), and Roxana: The Fortunate Mistress (1724) were written by Daniel Defoe.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 3 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following 18th-century narratives is NOT a philosophical or satirical prose tale?
items.explanation: The Mysteries of Udolpho (1794) by Ann Radcliffe is an archetype of high Gothic romance. Rasselas (Samuel Johnson), Candide (Voltaire), and Gulliver's Travels (Jonathan Swift) are philosophical and satirical allegories.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following Romantic poets was NOT part of the 'Lake School'?
items.explanation: Lord Byron belonged to the younger second generation of Romantics and famously mocked the Lake Poets in the Dedication to Don Juan. William Wordsworth, Samuel Taylor Coleridge, and Robert Southey formed the Lake School.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following Romantic poems was NOT one of John Keats's 1819 Great Odes?
items.explanation: Dejection: An Ode (1802) was written by Samuel Taylor Coleridge. Ode to a Nightingale, Ode on a Grecian Urn, and Ode on Melancholy are among the five famous spring 1819 odes composed by John Keats.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #3
items.meta: Gothic Romances of the Romantic Era
items.stem: Which of the following works is NOT a classic Gothic romance?
items.explanation: Sense and Sensibility (1811) by Jane Austen is a domestic novel of manners and moral realism. The Castle of Otranto (Walpole), The Mysteries of Udolpho (Radcliffe), and The Monk (Lewis) are foundational Gothic romances.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following poets was NOT a member of the younger 'Second Generation' of Romantics?
items.explanation: William Blake (born 1757) belonged to the older first generation/pre-Romantic period alongside Wordsworth and Coleridge. Lord Byron, Percy Bysshe Shelley, and John Keats were the younger second-generation Romantics.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following prose writers was NOT a major essayist of the Romantic era?
items.explanation: Walter Pater was a late Victorian Aesthetic critic and author of Studies in the History of the Renaissance (1873). Charles Lamb (Elia), William Hazlitt, and Thomas De Quincey were the leading essayists of the Romantic age.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #6
items.meta: Major Poetic Works of Percy Bysshe Shelley
items.stem: Which of the following major Romantic poetic works was NOT composed by Percy Bysshe Shelley?
items.explanation: Endymion (1818, 'A thing of beauty is a joy for ever') was composed by John Keats. Prometheus Unbound, Adonais (elegy for Keats), and The Masque of Anarchy were composed by Percy Bysshe Shelley.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following poems was NOT included in the landmark 1798 first edition of Lyrical Ballads?
options: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
items.explanation: The Prelude was Wordsworth's monumental autobiographical epic, begun in 1798 but left unpublished until after his death in 1850. The Ancient Mariner, Tintern Abbey, and The Idiot Boy all appeared in the 1798 Lyrical Ballads.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #8
items.meta: Sir Walter Scott's Waverley Historical Novels
items.stem: Which of the following Scottish historical novels was NOT written by Sir Walter Scott?
options: The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner
items.explanation: The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner (1824) was written by James Hogg. Waverley (1814), Rob Roy (1817), and The Heart of Midlothian (1818) are famous historical novels by Sir Walter Scott.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #9
items.stem: Which of the following literary periodicals was NOT founded during the Romantic era?
items.explanation: The Tatler was founded in 1709 during Queen Anne's reign by Richard Steele. The Edinburgh Review (1802), The Quarterly Review (1809), and Blackwood's Edinburgh Magazine (1817) were major 19th-century Romantic-era periodicals.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a major Romantic-era narrative poem or verse epic?
items.explanation: She Stoops to Conquer (1773) is an 18th-century 'laughing comedy' for the stage by Oliver Goldsmith. Don Juan (Byron), The Prelude (Wordsworth), and Endymion (Keats) are major Romantic narrative and epic poems.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following works is NOT classified among William Blake's illuminated 'Prophetic Books'?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
Songs of Innocence and of Experience
items.explanation: Songs of Innocence and of Experience (1794) is Blake's celebrated collection of lyric poems showing the 'Two Contrary States of the Human Soul'. Urizen, Jerusalem, and The Marriage of Heaven and Hell are complex Prophetic Books.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #12
items.stem: Which of the following Romantic narrative poems was NOT written by John Keats?
options: Isabella, or the Pot of Basil
items.explanation: The Revolt of Islam (1818) was composed in Spenserian stanzas by Percy Bysshe Shelley. The Eve of St. Agnes, Lamia, and Isabella, or the Pot of Basil are celebrated narrative verse romances by John Keats.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following 19th-century novels was NOT written by Jane Austen?
items.explanation: Wuthering Heights (1847) was written by Emily Brontë. Pride and Prejudice, Mansfield Park, and Northanger Abbey are three of the six core canonical novels of Jane Austen.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following figures was NOT attacked by Blackwood's Magazine as a member of the 'Cockney School'?
items.explanation: Robert Southey was a conservative Lake Poet and Tory Poet Laureate whom Byron labeled the 'Satanic School'. Leigh Hunt, John Keats, and William Hazlitt were the primary London targets of John Gibson Lockhart's 'Cockney School' attacks.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 4 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following poems is NOT classified among Samuel Taylor Coleridge's 'Conversation Poems'?
items.explanation: Kubla Khan is a visionary dream fragment poem. The Eolian Harp (1795), Frost at Midnight (1798), and This Lime-Tree Bower My Prison (1797) are Coleridge's celebrated blank-verse 'Conversation Poems'.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian novels is NOT set in Thomas Hardy's semi-fictional Wessex?
items.explanation: Middlemarch (1871–72) by George Eliot is set in a fictional provincial town in the English Midlands. The Return of the Native, The Mayor of Casterbridge, and Far from the Madding Crowd are Wessex novels by Thomas Hardy.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian literary figures was NOT associated with the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood?
items.explanation: Matthew Arnold was an Oxford-educated Victorian poet and cultural critic outside the Pre-Raphaelite movement. D. G. Rossetti (founder), Christina Rossetti, and William Morris were key Pre-Raphaelites.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian novels is NOT categorized as an industrial or 'Condition-of-England' novel?
items.explanation: Silas Marner (1861) by George Eliot is a pastoral moral fable set in rural Raveloe. Hard Times (Dickens), North and South (Gaskell), and Sybil, or The Two Nations (Disraeli) are benchmark Condition-of-England novels.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian poems is NOT a dramatic monologue by Robert Browning?
items.explanation: The Scholar-Gipsy (1853) is a reflective pastoral poem by Matthew Arnold. My Last Duchess (1842), Fra Lippo Lippi (1855), and Andrea del Sarto (1855) are masterpiece dramatic monologues by Robert Browning.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian women novelists was NOT one of the Brontë sisters?
items.explanation: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans. Charlotte Brontë (Jane Eyre), Emily Brontë (Wuthering Heights), and Anne Brontë (The Tenant of Wildfell Hall) were the three famous Brontë sisters of Haworth Parsonage.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian novels is NOT classified as a sensation novel?
items.explanation: Barchester Towers (1857) by Anthony Trollope is a comedic, provincial chronicle of ecclesiastical society. The Woman in White (Collins), East Lynne (Ellen Wood), and Lady Audley's Secret (Braddon) are quintessential sensation novels.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following Anthony Trollope novels does NOT belong to the 'Chronicles of Barsetshire' series?
items.explanation: The Way We Live Now (1875) is a standalone satirical masterpiece targeting London financial corruption. The Warden, Barchester Towers, and Doctor Thorne are early volumes in Trollope's 6-novel Barsetshire series.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian poems was NOT composed by Alfred, Lord Tennyson?
items.explanation: The Blessed Damozel (1850) was written and illustrated by Dante Gabriel Rossetti. In Memoriam A.H.H. (1850), The Lady of Shalott (1832/1842), and Ulysses (1842) are defining poems by Alfred, Lord Tennyson.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #9
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian figures was NOT a leader of the Oxford Movement (Tractarians)?
items.explanation: Thomas Carlyle was a Scottish Calvinist-influenced essayist and social critic. John Henry Newman, John Keble (whose 1833 'National Apostasy' sermon ignited the movement), and E. B. Pusey led the High Church Tractarian revival.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian intellectuals is NOT typically classified as a Victorian 'Sage Writer'?
items.explanation: Oscar Wilde was the premier playwright, novelist, and wit of late Victorian Aestheticism and Decadence. Thomas Carlyle (Sartor Resartus), John Ruskin (Unto This Last), and Matthew Arnold (Culture and Anarchy) are Victorian 'Sages'.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following 19th-century figures was NOT affiliated with Aestheticism or the Decadent movement?
items.explanation: Thomas Babington Macaulay was an early Victorian Whig historian, utilitarian, and essayist (Minute on Indian Education, 1835). Oscar Wilde, Walter Pater ('art for art's sake'), and Ernest Dowson were icons of Aestheticism and Decadence.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #12
items.meta: Charles Dickens's Early Picaresque / Comic Novels
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of Charles Dickens's early comic and episodic picaresque novels?
items.explanation: Our Mutual Friend (1864–65) is Dickens's last completed dark, panoramic social novel analyzing London's dust-heaps and materialism. The Pickwick Papers, Nicholas Nickleby, and Martin Chuzzlewit are earlier comic and picaresque works.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following Elizabeth Gaskell works is NOT focused on industrial conflict or fallen-woman social problems?
items.explanation: Cranford (1851–53) is a gentle, affectionate episodic chronicle of genteel spinster life in a rural village. Mary Barton (1848) and North and South (1855) tackle Manchester industrial strife, while Ruth (1853) addresses the unmarried mother.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian authors is NOT primarily celebrated for literary nonsense and comic verse?
items.explanation: Robert Louis Stevenson was an adventure, Gothic, and romance novelist (Treasure Island, Jekyll and Hyde). Lewis Carroll (Alice in Wonderland), Edward Lear (A Book of Nonsense), and W. S. Gilbert are masters of Victorian nonsense.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 5 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following Victorian realist novels was NOT written by George Eliot?
items.explanation: Agnes Grey (1847) was the debut governess novel by Anne Brontë. The Mill on the Floss (1860), Silas Marner (1861), and Daniel Deronda (1876) were written by George Eliot.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following modernist novels is NOT written using the stream-of-consciousness technique?
items.explanation: The Old Wives' Tale (1908) by Arnold Bennett is a classic Edwardian realist novel written in traditional chronological third-person narrative. Ulysses (Joyce), Mrs Dalloway (Woolf), and The Sound and the Fury (Faulkner) are quintessential stream-of-consciousness masterworks.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following 20th-century British authors was NOT a member of the Bloomsbury Group?
items.explanation: D. H. Lawrence was a working-class provincial outsider who intensely disliked the Bloomsbury circle after visiting Lady Ottoline Morrell and Bertrand Russell. Virginia Woolf, E. M. Forster, and biographer Lytton Strachey were central Bloomsbury Group figures.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following early 20th-century poets was NOT part of the Imagist movement?
items.explanation: Rupert Brooke was a Georgian romantic poet famous for patriotic wartime sonnets like 'The Soldier'. Ezra Pound, H. D. (Hilda Doolittle), and Richard Aldington launched Imagism in London in 1912.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #4
items.meta: World War I Frontline Soldier Poets
items.stem: Which of the following poets was NOT a frontline soldier poet of the First World War?
items.explanation: W. H. Auden was only eleven years old when World War I ended in 1918; he became the voice of the 1930s generation. Wilfred Owen, Siegfried Sassoon, and Isaac Rosenberg fought in the trenches of the Western Front and wrote anti-war combat poetry.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following 1930s British poets was NOT considered a member of the 'Auden Generation'?
items.explanation: Dylan Thomas was a Neo-Romantic, Welsh lyric poet associated with the New Apocalypse movement, rejecting the detached social-political verse of the 1930s. W. H. Auden, Stephen Spender, and Cecil Day-Lewis formed the core 'Macspaunday' / Pylon group.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following poems is NOT a major High Modernist multi-part long poem?
items.explanation: The Ballad of Reading Gaol (1898) by Oscar Wilde is a late Victorian narrative ballad in traditional six-line stanzas. The Waste Land (Eliot), The Cantos (Pound), and The Bridge (Hart Crane) are fragmented High Modernist epics.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #7
items.meta: Architects of the Irish Literary Revival
items.stem: Which of the following Irish dramatists was NOT a central architect of the Irish Literary Revival at the Abbey Theatre?
items.explanation: George Bernard Shaw was a London-based Fabian socialist and master of British intellectual comedies, maintaining distance from the Dublin Celtic Revival. W. B. Yeats, Lady Augusta Gregory, and J. M. Synge co-founded and built the Irish National Theatre Society (Abbey Theatre).

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #8
items.meta: Critical Concepts of T. S. Eliot
items.stem: Which of the following famous critical concepts was NOT formulated by T. S. Eliot?
items.explanation: Negative Capability was coined by the Romantic poet John Keats in an 1817 letter to his brothers. Objective Correlative ('Hamlet and His Problems'), Dissociation of Sensibility ('The Metaphysical Poets'), and Impersonality of Poetry ('Tradition and the Individual Talent') are all by T. S. Eliot.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #9
items.stem: Which of the following landmark modernist works was NOT written by James Joyce?
options: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
items.explanation: The Waves (1931) is an experimental poetic novel written by Virginia Woolf. Dubliners (1914), A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (1916), and Finnegans Wake (1939) are monumental prose works by James Joyce.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following modernist novels or novellas was NOT written by Joseph Conrad?
items.explanation: A Passage to India (1924) was written by E. M. Forster. Heart of Darkness (1899), Lord Jim (1900), and Nostromo (1904) are celebrated sea and imperial political novels by Joseph Conrad.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #11
items.meta: Major Novels of D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Which of the following 20th-century novels was NOT written by D. H. Lawrence?
items.explanation: Point Counter Point (1928) is a satirical novel of ideas by Aldous Huxley (which actually features a character, Mark Rampion, modeled on Lawrence). Sons and Lovers (1913), The Rainbow (1915), and Women in Love (1920) are major novels by D. H. Lawrence.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #12
items.stem: Which of the following periodicals was NOT a 20th-century modernist avant-garde little magazine?
items.explanation: The Yellow Book (1894–97) was an 1890s Aesthetic and Decadent quarterly associated with Aubrey Beardsley. Blast (Wyndham Lewis's Vorticism), The Egoist (edited by Harriet Shaw Weaver), and The Criterion (founded by T. S. Eliot) were 20th-century modernist journals.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following authors was NOT one of the Edwardian 'materialist' novelists criticized by Virginia Woolf in 'Modern Fiction'?
items.explanation: Virginia Woolf wrote the 1919 essay 'Modern Fiction' precisely to attack the Edwardian 'materialists' for focusing on external house-property and trivial details instead of the 'luminous halo' of consciousness. The three authors she attacked were Arnold Bennett, John Galsworthy, and H. G. Wells.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following American modernist writers was NOT associated with the 1920s Parisian 'Lost Generation' circle?
items.explanation: Robert Frost lived in England briefly (1912–15) before returning to farm in New Hampshire and Vermont, remaining independent of the Paris expatriate scene. Ernest Hemingway, F. Scott Fitzgerald, and salon leader Gertrude Stein defined the 'Lost Generation' in 1920s Paris.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 6 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following theatrical figures was NOT a 20th-century modernist avant-garde theatrical pioneer?
items.explanation: Sir Arthur Wing Pinero was a late Victorian and Edwardian master of the conventional commercial 'Well-Made Play' (The Second Mrs Tanqueray). Bertolt Brecht (Epic Theatre), Luigi Pirandello (Metatheatre), and Antonin Artaud (Theatre of Cruelty) revolutionized modernist drama.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following post-war dramatists is NOT associated with the Theatre of the Absurd?
items.explanation: John Osborne was the leader of the British 'Angry Young Men' and Social Realism (Look Back in Anger). Samuel Beckett, Eugène Ionesco, and Harold Pinter are defining dramatists analyzed in Martin Esslin's seminal study The Theatre of the Absurd (1961).

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following 1950s British literary figures was NOT associated with the 'Angry Young Men'?
items.explanation: Philip Larkin was the leading poet of 'The Movement' and explicitly distanced himself from the bohemian rebellion of the Angry Young Men. John Osborne (Look Back in Anger), Kingsley Amis (Lucky Jim), and Alan Sillitoe (Saturday Night and Sunday Morning) were the icons of the AYM.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following post-war poets was NOT a member of the British group 'The Movement'?
items.explanation: Allen Ginsberg was an American countercultural Beat Generation poet (Howl). Philip Larkin, Thom Gunn, and Donald Davie were featured in Robert Conquest's 1956 anthology New Lines, which established 'The Movement' in Britain.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following American poets is NOT classified as a Confessional poet?
items.explanation: Wallace Stevens was a High Modernist poet celebrated for philosophical, aesthetic lyrics (Harmonium). Robert Lowell (Life Studies, which coined the genre), Sylvia Plath (Ariel), and Anne Sexton (Live or Die) were pioneering Confessional poets.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following post-war American authors was NOT associated with the 'Beat Generation'?
items.explanation: John Updike was an elegant, mainstream realist novelist chronicling suburban American middle-class life (Rabbit, Run). Jack Kerouac (On the Road), Allen Ginsberg (Howl), and William S. Burroughs (Naked Lunch) were the core trio of the Beat Generation.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following post-war American poets was NOT one of the Black Mountain Poets?
items.explanation: Frank O'Hara was a leader of the New York School of poets, known for his spontaneous urban 'I Do This, I Do That' poems. Charles Olson (author of 'Projective Verse'), Robert Creeley, and Robert Duncan were core Black Mountain Poets.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following British dramatists was NOT associated with 1990s 'In-Yer-Face Theatre'?
items.explanation: Terence Rattigan was a mid-20th-century master of discreet, repressed British Well-Made Plays (The Deep Blue Sea). Sarah Kane (Blasted), Mark Ravenhill (Shopping and Fucking), and Anthony Neilson pioneered 1990s In-Yer-Face Theatre (as theorized by Aleks Sierz).

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following post-war stage plays is NOT an example of British Kitchen Sink Realism?
items.explanation: Waiting for Godot (1953) by Samuel Beckett is an avant-garde Absurdist drama set in an empty landscape. Look Back in Anger (Osborne), A Taste of Honey (Shelagh Delaney), and Roots (Arnold Wesker) are classic Kitchen Sink realist plays set in working-class interiors.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #9
items.stem: Which of the following plays is NOT classified among Harold Pinter's early 'Comedies of Menace'?
items.explanation: Betrayal (1978) is a later memory play by Harold Pinter that uses reverse chronology to explore an extramarital affair. The Birthday Party (1957), The Caretaker (1960), and The Dumb Waiter (1957) are his celebrated early 'Comedies of Menace'.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following post-war British novels is NOT structured primarily around historiographic metafiction or self-reflexive narrative?
items.explanation: The Remains of the Day (1989) by Kazuo Ishiguro is an understated psychological study of repression narrated by an unreliable butler. The French Lieutenant's Woman (Fowles), Possession (Byatt), and Waterland (Swift) are premier works of British historiographic metafiction.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following post-war plays was NOT written by Samuel Beckett?
items.explanation: The Homecoming (1965) is a major play by Harold Pinter. Waiting for Godot (1953), Endgame (1957), and Krapp's Last Tape (1958) are seminal absurdist theatrical masterpieces written by Samuel Beckett.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #12
items.stem: Which of the following British intellectual dramas was NOT written by Tom Stoppard?
items.explanation: Equus (1973) is a psychological drama written by Peter Shaffer. Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead (1966), Jumpers (1972), and Arcadia (1993) are celebrated witty, philosophically complex dramas by Tom Stoppard.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following post-war British novels is NOT a dark dystopian or allegorical narrative?
items.explanation: Lucky Jim (1954) by Kingsley Amis is a light-hearted comic campus novel following the misadventures of Jim Dixon. Nineteen Eighty-Four (Orwell), Lord of the Flies (Golding), and A Clockwork Orange (Burgess) are famous dystopian/allegorical warnings.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following American poets was NOT a central member of the New York School?
items.explanation: Charles Bukowski was a Los Angeles-based 'dirty realist' and outsider poet completely detached from the art-world aesthetics of New York. Frank O'Hara, John Ashbery, and Kenneth Koch formed the core first generation of the New York School.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 7 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following feminist stage works was NOT written by Caryl Churchill?
items.explanation: Blasted (1995) is a controversial In-Yer-Face play written by Sarah Kane. Top Girls (1982), Cloud Nine (1979), and Vinegar Tom (1976) are seminal feminist and socialist theatrical works by Caryl Churchill.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #1
items.meta: The Founding Trio of Indian English Fiction
items.stem: Which of the following literary figures was NOT one of the 'Founding Trio' of the Indian English novel?
items.explanation: Nissim Ezekiel was a major post-independence Indian English poet, playwright, and critic. Mulk Raj Anand (Untouchable), R. K. Narayan (Swami and Friends), and Raja Rao (Kanthapura) are universally recognized as the 'Big Three' or Founding Trio of Indian English fiction.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following novels is NOT a narrative centered on the 1947 Partition of India?
items.explanation: The Guide (1958) by R. K. Narayan is a comic and philosophical tale of Raju's spiritual transformation set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi. Train to Pakistan (Khushwant Singh), Azadi (Chaman Nahal), and Ice-Candy-Man (Bapsi Sidhwa) are landmark Partition novels.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following novels by Amitav Ghosh does NOT belong to the 'Ibis Trilogy'?
items.explanation: The Glass Palace (2000) is a standalone historical epic spanning Burma, Bengal, and Malaya. Sea of Poppies (2008), River of Smoke (2011), and Flood of Fire (2015) comprise Amitav Ghosh's celebrated Ibis Trilogy dealing with the 19th-century opium trade.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following poetry collections was NOT written by Nissim Ezekiel?
items.explanation: The Striders (1966) was the debut poetry collection of A. K. Ramanujan. A Time to Change (1952), The Exact Name (1965), and Hymns in Darkness (1976) are landmark poetry collections by Nissim Ezekiel.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following was NOT a post-independence modern Indian English poet?
items.explanation: Toru Dutt was a 19th-century colonial-era bilingual poet and translator who died in 1877 (author of A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields and Ancient Ballads and Legends of Hindustan). Nissim Ezekiel, Dom Moraes, and Adil Jussawalla were modern post-independence poets.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following Indian English novels was NOT written by R. K. Narayan?
items.explanation: Untouchable (1935) was written by Mulk Raj Anand with a preface by E. M. Forster. Swami and Friends (1935), The Bachelor of Arts (1937), and The English Teacher (1945) form R. K. Narayan's famous semi-autobiographical Malgudi trilogy.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following acclaimed novels was NOT written by Salman Rushdie?
items.explanation: The English Patient (1992) was written by Sri Lankan-Canadian novelist Michael Ondaatje. Midnight's Children (1981), Shame (1983), and The Satanic Verses (1988) are major novels by Salman Rushdie.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following poets was NOT a post-1960s modern Indian English feminist or confessional poet?
items.explanation: Sarojini Naidu ('The Nightingale of India') was an early 20th-century lyric poet and freedom fighter writing in romantic, nationalist modes. Kamala Das (Summer in Calcutta), Eunice de Souza (Fix), and Imtiaz Dharker (Purdah) are modern post-independence feminist voices.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #9
items.meta: Sahitya Akademi Award-Winning Novels in English
items.stem: Which of the following celebrated novels did NOT win the Sahitya Akademi Award in English?
items.explanation: Midnight's Children by Salman Rushdie won the Booker Prize (1981) and Booker of Bookers, but never won the Sahitya Akademi Award. The Guide (Narayan, 1960), The Serpent and the Rope (Raja Rao, 1964), and The Shadow Lines (Amitav Ghosh, 1989) all won the Sahitya Akademi Award.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following psychological novels was NOT written by Anita Desai?
items.explanation: The God of Small Things (1997) is the Booker Prize-winning debut novel by Arundhati Roy. Cry, the Peacock (1963), Clear Light of Day (1980), and Fire on the Mountain (1977, Sahitya Akademi Award) are major novels by Anita Desai.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #11
items.meta: Social-Protest Fiction of Mulk Raj Anand
items.stem: Which of the following 1930s social-realist novels was NOT written by Mulk Raj Anand?
items.explanation: Kanthapura (1938) is Raja Rao's Gandhian sthala-purana set in a South Indian village. Untouchable (1935), Coolie (1936), and Two Leaves and a Bud (1937) form Mulk Raj Anand's trilogy of social protest exposing caste and capitalist exploitation.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #12
items.meta: Works and Translations by A. K. Ramanujan
items.stem: Which of the following poetry or translation volumes was NOT authored by A. K. Ramanujan?
items.explanation: Jejuri (1976) is a Commonwealth Poetry Prize-winning collection by Arun Kolatkar about a pilgrimage to a temple town in Maharashtra. The Striders (1966), Relations (1971), and Speaking of Siva (1973) were created by A. K. Ramanujan.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #13
items.meta: Satirical and Comic Indian English Novels
items.stem: Which of the following Indian novels is NOT a satirical, academic, or bureaucratic comic narrative?
items.explanation: Fasting, Feasting (1999) by Anita Desai is an intimate, serious domestic psychological novel contrasting Indian and American family expectations. English, August (Chatterjee), The Great Indian Novel (Tharoor), and Chronicle of a Corpse Bearer (Kanga) are satirical/comic narratives.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #14
items.meta: Indian Diasporic Women Novelists in North America
items.stem: Which of the following Indian diasporic authors was NOT primarily based in North America (USA)?
items.explanation: Kamala Markandaya (author of Nectar in a Sieve) emigrated to Britain in 1948 and spent her entire literary career in London. Jhumpa Lahiri, Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni, and Bharati Mukherjee built their literary reputations in the United States.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 8 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following Indian English novels did NOT win the Booker Prize?
items.explanation: A Suitable Boy (1993) by Vikram Seth was famously overlooked and not even shortlisted for the Booker Prize. Midnight's Children (Rushdie, 1981), The God of Small Things (Roy, 1997), and The White Tiger (Adiga, 2008) are Booker Prize winners.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following postcolonial literary figures was NOT an African novelist?
items.explanation: Derek Walcott was a Saint Lucian Caribbean poet and playwright who won the 1992 Nobel Prize in Literature (author of Omeros). Chinua Achebe (Nigeria), Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o (Kenya), and Ayi Kwei Armah (Ghana) are pioneer African novelists.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following celebrated postcolonial writers was NOT from the Caribbean?
items.explanation: Wole Soyinka is a Nigerian dramatist, poet, and critic who became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986. Derek Walcott (Saint Lucia), V. S. Naipaul (Trinidad), and George Lamming (Barbados) are giants of Caribbean literature.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following novels does NOT belong to Chinua Achebe's famous 'African Trilogy'?
items.explanation: Petals of Blood (1977) was written by Kenyan author Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o. Things Fall Apart (1958), No Longer at Ease (1960), and Arrow of God (1964) comprise Chinua Achebe's canonical African Trilogy documenting Igbo society.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following theorists is NOT part of the foundational 'Holy Trinity' of Postcolonial Theory?
items.explanation: Fredric Jameson is an American Marxist literary critic and theorist of Postmodernism (Postmodernism, or, the Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism). Edward Said (Orientalism), Homi Bhabha (The Location of Culture), and Gayatri Spivak constitute the 'Holy Trinity' of Postcolonial Theory.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following figures was NOT a core novelist of the 1960s Latin American 'Boom'?
items.explanation: Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian novelist and father of modern African literature. Gabriel García Márquez (Colombia), Mario Vargas Llosa (Peru), and Julio Cortázar (Argentina) were leading novelists of the 1960s Latin American 'Boom'.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following celebrated Commonwealth writers was NOT a Canadian author?
items.explanation: Patrick White was an Australian novelist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1973 (Voss). Margaret Atwood (The Handmaid's Tale), Alice Munro (Nobel 2013), and Michael Ondaatje (The English Patient) are eminent Canadian literary figures.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following acclaimed novels is NOT a work of Australian literature?
items.explanation: Disgrace (1999) is set in post-apartheid South Africa and was written by South African author J. M. Coetzee. Voss (1957) and The Tree of Man (1955) by Patrick White, and Oscar and Lucinda (1988) by Peter Carey, are Australian classics.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following literary figures was NOT one of the three original founders of the Négritude movement?
items.explanation: Frantz Fanon was a Martinican psychiatrist, revolutionary theorist, and author of Black Skin, White Masks and The Wretched of the Earth, who offered critical appraisals of Négritude. Aimé Césaire, Léopold Sédar Senghor, and Léon Damas co-founded Négritude in 1930s Paris.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #9
items.meta: Booker Prize Winners Connected to Africa
items.stem: Which of the following African literary classics did NOT win the Booker Prize?
items.explanation: Things Fall Apart was published in 1958, eleven years before the Booker Prize was instituted in 1969. In a Free State (Naipaul, 1971, set in Africa), The Famished Road (Ben Okri, 1991), and Disgrace (Coetzee, 1999) all won the Booker Prize.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #10
items.meta: Major Novels by Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
items.stem: Which of the following East African novels was NOT written by Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o?
options: The Beautyful Ones Are Not Yet Born
items.explanation: The Beautyful Ones Are Not Yet Born (1968) was written by Ghanaian novelist Ayi Kwei Armah. Weep Not, Child (1964), A Grain of Wheat (1967), and Petals of Blood (1977) are major novels by Kenyan author Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following authors was NOT a South African anti-apartheid novelist?
items.explanation: Ben Okri is a Nigerian novelist and poet based in London (The Famished Road). Nadine Gordimer (Burger's Daughter), J. M. Coetzee (Waiting for the Barbarians), and André Brink (A Dry White Season) were prominent South African novelists confronting apartheid.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #12
items.meta: Postcolonial Rewritings of the Western Canon
items.stem: Which of the following is the original European canonical work rather than a postcolonial rewriting?
items.explanation: Heart of Darkness (1899) is Joseph Conrad's original colonial novella. Wide Sargasso Sea (Jean Rhys rewrites Jane Eyre), Foe (J. M. Coetzee rewrites Robinson Crusoe), and Une Tempête (Aimé Césaire rewrites The Tempest) are postcolonial 'writing back' counter-texts.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #13
items.meta: Caribbean Nation Language and Dub Poets
items.stem: Which of the following poets was NOT an Anglo-Caribbean poet known for nation language or dub poetry?
items.explanation: Langston Hughes was an African-American poet and central leader of the 1920s Harlem Renaissance. Kamau Brathwaite (Barbados, theorist of 'nation language'), Louise Bennett ('Miss Lou', Jamaica), and Linton Kwesi Johnson (Jamaica/UK, dub poetry) are Anglo-Caribbean poets.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #14
items.stem: Which of the following African dramas was NOT written by Wole Soyinka?
items.explanation: The Blood Knot (1961) is an anti-apartheid drama written by South African playwright Athol Fugard. Death and the King's Horseman, The Lion and the Jewel, and A Dance of the Forests are masterpiece dramas by Nigerian Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 9 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following feminist writers was NOT an African novelist?
items.explanation: Alice Walker is an African-American novelist and essayist who coined the term 'Womanism' (The Color Purple). Flora Nwapa (Efuru, Nigeria), Buchi Emecheta (The Joys of Motherhood, Nigeria), and Ama Ata Aidoo (Our Sister Killjoy, Ghana) are African women writers.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #1
items.stem: Which of the following critical figures was NOT a Russian Formalist?
items.explanation: Roland Barthes was a French Structuralist and Post-structuralist critic (Mythologies, 'The Death of the Author'). Viktor Shklovsky ('Art as Technique' / defamiliarization), Roman Jakobson, and Boris Eikhenbaum were foundational Russian Formalists of OPOJAZ and the Moscow Linguistic Circle.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #2
items.stem: Which of the following mid-century American critics was NOT associated with the New Criticism?
items.explanation: R. S. Crane was the leader of the Chicago Neo-Aristotelians (Critics and Criticism), who vigorously contested the New Critics' method. Cleanth Brooks (The Well Wrought Urn), W. K. Wimsatt (The Verbal Icon), and John Crowe Ransom (The New Criticism) were New Critics.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #3
items.stem: Which of the following philosophers was NOT associated with the Frankfurt School of Critical Theory?
items.explanation: Jacques Derrida was an Algerian-born French philosopher who founded Deconstruction (Of Grammatology). Theodor Adorno, Max Horkheimer (Dialectic of Enlightenment), and Walter Benjamin were central figures of the Marxist Frankfurt School of Critical Theory.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #4
items.stem: Which of the following literary theorists was NOT a member of the 'Yale School' of Deconstruction?
items.explanation: Stanley Fish is a pioneer of Reader-Response Criticism and the concept of 'interpretive communities' (Is There a Text in This Class?). Paul de Man, J. Hillis Miller, Geoffrey Hartman, and Harold Bloom (with Jacques Derrida) formed the Yale School of Deconstruction.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #5
items.stem: Which of the following scholars was NOT a proponent of Reader-Response Criticism or Reception Theory?
items.explanation: Ferdinand de Saussure was a Swiss linguist whose Course in General Linguistics (1916) founded modern structural linguistics. Wolfgang Iser ('implied reader', gaps), Hans Robert Jauss ('horizon of expectations'), and Stanley Fish are giants of Reader-Response criticism.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #6
items.stem: Which of the following feminist theorists was NOT a proponent of French psychoanalytic 'Écriture Féminine'?
items.explanation: Elaine Showalter is an American feminist critic who developed 'Gynocritics' and the three historical phases of women's writing (A Literature of Their Own). Hélène Cixous ('The Laugh of the Medusa'), Luce Irigaray (Speculum of the Other Woman), and Julia Kristeva pioneered French feminist theory.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #7
items.stem: Which of the following thinkers is NOT strictly classified as a Classical Structuralist?
items.explanation: Michel Foucault is a seminal Post-structuralist philosopher who rejected structuralism's universal timeless patterns to study historical shifts in power, discipline, and discourse (epistemes). Saussure (linguistics), Lévi-Strauss (anthropology), and Genette (narratology) are structuralists.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #8
items.stem: Which of the following critical theorists is NOT primarily recognized for foundational contributions to Postcolonial Theory?
items.explanation: Stephen Greenblatt is the leading pioneer and theorist of New Historicism / Cultural Poetics (Renaissance Self-Fashioning). Edward Said (Orientalism), Homi K. Bhabha (The Location of Culture), and Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak are the primary architects of Postcolonial Theory.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #9
items.meta: New Historicism and Cultural Materialism Theorists
items.stem: Which of the following literary critics was NOT associated with New Historicism or Cultural Materialism?
items.explanation: Harold Bloom was an unapologetic aesthetic individualist who defended the Western Canon and proposed the Oedipal theory of 'The Anxiety of Influence'. Stephen Greenblatt, Louis Montrose ('the historicity of texts and the textuality of history'), and Alan Sinfield are New Historicist/Materialist critics.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #10
items.stem: Which of the following major theorists was NOT a Marxist literary critic?
items.explanation: Cleanth Brooks was a formalist New Critic who advocated for the autonomy of the poem and close reading of irony and paradox (The Well Wrought Urn). Georg Lukács (The Historical Novel), Terry Eagleton (Marxism and Literary Criticism), and Fredric Jameson are Marxist critics.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #11
items.stem: Which of the following thinkers was NOT primarily a psychoanalytic theorist?
items.explanation: Northrop Frye was a Canadian literary theorist who established Archetypal Criticism (Anatomy of Criticism, 1957). Sigmund Freud (id/ego/superego, Oedipus complex), Jacques Lacan (mirror stage, the unconscious structured like a language), and Carl Jung (collective unconscious) are psychoanalytic titans.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #12
items.stem: Which of the following figures was NOT a pioneer of Archetypal or Myth Criticism?
items.explanation: Roman Jakobson was a Russian Formalist and Structuralist linguist who analyzed metaphor, metonymy, and poetic function. Northrop Frye (Anatomy of Criticism), Maud Bodkin (Archetypal Patterns in Poetry), and Joseph Campbell (The Hero with a Thousand Faces) are Archetypal critics.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #13
items.stem: Which of the following foundational literary critics was NOT a Classical antiquity theorist?
items.explanation: Sir Philip Sidney was an English Renaissance humanist courtier and critic who wrote An Apology for Poetry (c. 1580, pub. 1595). Plato (The Republic), Aristotle (Poetics), and Longinus (On the Sublime) were foundational critics of Greco-Roman antiquity.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #14
items.meta: Semiotic and Structuralist Works by Roland Barthes
items.stem: Which of the following seminal critical texts was NOT written by Roland Barthes?
items.explanation: Of Grammatology (De la grammatologie, 1967) was written by Jacques Derrida, introducing deconstructive critique of phonocentrism and logocentrism. Mythologies (1957), S/Z (1970), and The Fashion System (1967) are famous semiotic and structuralist texts by Roland Barthes.

items.title: Game 8 (🧩 Odd One Out) · Level 10 · Set #15
items.stem: Which of the following critical concepts does NOT belong to Derridean Post-structuralism and Deconstruction?
options: Il n'y a pas de hors-texte
items.explanation: Objective Correlative is a modernist critical term coined by Washington Allston and famously applied to Hamlet by T. S. Eliot in 1919. Différance, Aporia (the impasse of undecidability), and 'Il n'y a pas de hors-texte' ('There is no outside-text') are fundamental Derridean deconstructive concepts.
